title: RDS & Aurora High Availability
summary: Multi-AZ, read replicas, Aurora replicas and Global Database for resilient relational data.
tldr: **Multi-AZ** is for availability: a synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover. A classic Multi-AZ *instance* standby can't serve reads.
**Read replicas** are for read scaling (and cross-Region DR): asynchronous, readable, and promoted *manually*.
**Aurora** keeps six copies of data across three AZs. Add **Aurora Replicas** in other AZs so failover takes about a minute or less; use **Global Database** for cross-Region DR with sub-second lag.
Logical mistakes (bad UPDATE, corruption) need **point-in-time restore** or **Aurora Backtrack**, not replicas, which copy the mistake.

keyFacts.text: Typical failover for an **RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster** (one writer + two *readable* standbys in three AZs), versus 1–2 minutes for a Multi-AZ DB instance.
Aurora Replicas per cluster. Each has a **promotion tier 0–15**; Aurora promotes the lowest tier first, so put a full-size replica in tier 0.
**Aurora Global Database**: storage-level replication with typical lag under a second and cross-Region failover in about a minute. Up to 10 secondary Regions.
Automated backup retention for RDS and Aurora, giving point-in-time restore to a *new* instance or cluster. Longer retention needs manual snapshots or AWS Backup.
Longest **Aurora Backtrack** window (Aurora MySQL only). It rewinds the *same* cluster in minutes, with no new endpoint.

traps: The standby of a Multi-AZ **DB instance** can't take read traffic. Reporting tools need a read replica or a Multi-AZ DB cluster.
A read replica is **not** automatic failover. It needs manual promotion and gets a new endpoint.
Global Database is Aurora-only. You can't add an RDS for PostgreSQL instance to it; use a cross-Region read replica instead.
**Managed failover** is for an unplanned outage. A planned Region move with zero data loss is a **switchover**.
Replicas and Multi-AZ copy bad writes instantly. Recovering from human error needs PITR, snapshots or Backtrack.
Increasing `max_connections` or the instance size doesn't fix connection storms from Lambda. RDS Proxy pools connections and also shortens failover.

sections.heading: Aurora endpoints
sections.body:
- **Cluster (writer) endpoint**: always points to the current writer.
- **Reader endpoint**: load-balances across all Aurora Replicas.
- **Custom endpoint**: a group of instances you choose, for example small replicas for analysts only.
- **Instance endpoint**: one specific instance, rarely the right exam answer.
